# Web Platform: mobile-web.md

Self-contained. The skill's rules, then this topic, then anything it relies on from other skills.

## Skill rules

How I build for the web: browser-native HTML, CSS and JS, the Next.js App Router, Astro, and Supabase auth. Plus the accessibility, performance, security and visual details that separate hand-built work from component-library output.

Evergreen browsers only. No legacy prefixes. No polyfills for anything above 95% support. Mobile-first: build for a mid-range Android phone on a cell network, not a desktop monitor.

JavaScript causes most performance problems. Load less of it. Move logic to the server. If CSS or HTML can do it, that's where it goes.

### Rules for Every Web Task

**CSS layer order.** Declare it once at the top of the root stylesheet. A later layer beats an earlier one regardless of specificity:

```css
@layer reset, base, tokens, components, utilities, overrides;
```

**Tokens live in one `:root` block.** Color, spacing, type, radius, shadow and motion all reference custom properties named after the design file's token paths (`--color-semantic-text-primary`). No raw values in component rules. Colors are `oklch()`.

**Animate `transform` and `opacity`.** They composite. `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin` and `padding` run layout every frame. Motion values come from the design or `motion-design`. Don't invent them. Write motion inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.

**Server Components are the Next.js default.** `"use client"` only for state, effects, event handlers or browser APIs. Keep it at the leaves.

**Request APIs are async.** Await `cookies()`, `headers()`, `draftMode()`, `params` and `searchParams`. Request interception lives in `proxy.ts`.

**Caching is explicit.** With Cache Components on, nothing is cached unless it's marked `"use cache"`. Anything that reads request data or uncached data sits inside `<Suspense>`.

**Every input has a `<label>`.** Validate on the server, always. Client-side validation is UX, not security.

**Lane rules.** Vercel is frontend only. Publishable key, RLS enforced, the secret key never touches it. The publishable key goes through `@supabase/ssr` with the user's cookie session, and RLS via `auth.uid()` is the security boundary. A query that needs the secret key belongs on Railway behind an API endpoint. Every Server Function verifies the user itself, because it's reachable by direct POST.

**Support policy.** Baseline widely available: use it freely. Newly available: use it, with an `@supports` or feature-detected fallback only where a miss would break function, not polish. Limited availability: progressive enhancement only. Check `reference/browser-compatibility.md` before reaching for anything newer than container queries.

### Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Why it's wrong |
| --- | --- |
| JS-computed sizing or scroll listeners where container queries or scroll-driven animations do the job | Layout reads force reflow on the main thread |
| `outline: none` with no replacement | Fails WCAG 2.4.7 |
| `user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale=1` | Blocks zoom. WCAG 1.4.4 |
| `html { font-size: <16px }` or the `62.5%` rem hack | Overrides the user's font-size preference |
| Placeholder text as a label | Disappears on input and isn't a dependable accessible name |
| Infinite scroll with no alternative | Keyboard and screen-reader users lose the footer and their place |
| `loading="lazy"` on the LCP image, or no `fetchpriority="high"` on it | Directly hurts LCP |
| `revalidateTag("tag")` with one argument | Type error. Pass a profile: `revalidateTag("tag", "max")` |
| `priority` on `next/image` | Not the prop. The LCP image takes `fetchPriority="high"` with `loading="eager"` |
| Plain `@supabase/supabase-js` client in server code on Vercel | No cookie session, no refresh. Use `@supabase/ssr` |
| `getSession()` to authorize on the server | Reads the cookie without verifying it. Use `getClaims()` |
| `proxy.ts` as the only auth check | A matcher change silently removes it. Check in the page and the Server Function too |
| Per-user data inside a shared `"use cache"` | Replayed with no RLS check |
| `z` from `astro:content`, or `entry.render()` | `z` is from `astro/zod`. `render()` is imported from `astro:content` |

### Mobile-First CSS

Write the smallest layout first and add to it with `@media (width >= ...)`. The base rules are then the ones the slowest devices parse.

- Breakpoints in `rem`, so they respond to the user's font size as well as the screen.
- Media queries for page layout, container queries for components (`css.md`).
- Logical properties (`margin-inline`, `padding-block`, `inset-inline-start`), so layouts hold in right-to-left languages.
- Google indexes the mobile version. Content hidden or missing on mobile is missing from search.

### Touch Targets

44 by 44 CSS px (Apple) or 48 by 48 (Material) for anything tapped with a finger. WCAG 2.2 AA's floor is 24 by 24 (2.5.8). That's a legal minimum, not a comfortable size. Grow the hit area with padding, not the icon. Inline links inside a sentence are exempt. Standalone links and buttons aren't.

```css
.icon-button {
    display: grid;
    place-items: center;
    min-inline-size: var(--size-target-min);
    min-block-size: var(--size-target-min);
}
```

### Viewport and Safe Areas

The viewport meta is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`. Nothing that blocks zoom. For an edge-to-edge design, add `viewport-fit=cover` and pad with the safe-area insets:

```css
.bottom-nav {
    padding-block-end: max(var(--spacing-2), env(safe-area-inset-bottom));
    padding-inline: max(var(--spacing-4), env(safe-area-inset-left)) max(var(--spacing-4), env(safe-area-inset-right));
}
```

iOS Safari zooms the page when a focused input's font size is under 16px. The fix is a 16px or larger input font. Never disable zoom.

### Touch and Pointer Input

```css
/* Hover styles only where hover exists, so they don't stick after a tap */
@media (hover: hover) {
    .card:hover { translate: 0 calc(-1 * var(--motion-distance-sm)); }
}

/* Controls: no double-tap zoom, no accidental text selection */
button, [role="button"] {
    touch-action: manipulation;
    -webkit-user-select: none; /* Safari still needs the prefix */
    user-select: none;
}

/* A scrollable panel that doesn't scroll the page behind it at its edges */
.sheet-body {
    overflow-y: auto;
    overscroll-behavior: contain;
}
```

- Use Pointer Events (`pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`, `pointercancel`). One set of handlers for mouse, touch and pen.
- Always handle `pointercancel`. The browser fires it when it takes over the gesture for scrolling. A drag that ignores it gets stuck.
- Call `element.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)` on `pointerdown`, so a drag keeps receiving events after the pointer leaves the element.
- Set `touch-action` on a draggable element (`none`, or `pan-y` for a horizontal carousel). That replaces `preventDefault()` in a non-passive touch listener.
- Anything done by dragging also has a tap or button alternative (WCAG 2.5.7). Nothing is reachable by hover alone.

### Base Font Size

Never set a root font size below the default. Never fix it in `px`. Users change the default, and `rem` only respects that if the root is left alone.

```css
/* Correct */
html { font-size: 100%; }

/* Wrong */
html { font-size: 14px; }
html { font-size: 62.5%; }   /* the "1rem = 10px" hack: shrinks everything for users who raised their default */
```

### Progressive Web Apps

Add a manifest and service worker only when installability or offline use is a requirement in the spec. A service worker is a second cache layer on top of the framework's.

```json
{
    "name": "App Name",
    "short_name": "App",
    "id": "/",
    "start_url": "/",
    "display": "standalone",
    "background_color": "#1a1a1a",
    "theme_color": "#1a1a1a",
    "icons": [
        { "src": "/icons/192.png", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png" },
        { "src": "/icons/512.png", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png" },
        { "src": "/icons/512-maskable.png", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png", "purpose": "maskable" }
    ]
}
```

- The manifest is JSON and can't read CSS variables. Its two colors are the one place hex is written by hand. Keep them equal to the background token. In Next.js, generate the manifest from `app/manifest.ts`.
- The maskable icon is a separate entry. An icon declared only as maskable gets cropped where masks aren't used.
- `shortcuts` and `orientation` don't work on iOS. Install there is manual (Share, then Add to Home Screen), there's no install prompt event, and web push only works for an installed app.

Service worker rules:

- Network-first for navigations with an offline page as the fallback. Cache-first for hashed static assets.
- Version the cache name per deploy and delete old caches on `activate`, or users keep stale assets forever.
- Never cache authenticated or per-user responses. Never intercept non-GET requests.
